The '''Metropolitan Detention Center, Guaynabo (MDC Guaynabo)''' is a United States [[federal prison]] facility in [[Guaynabo, Puerto Rico]]. It holds male and female inmates of all security levels who are awaiting trial or sentencing. It is operated by the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], a division of the [[United States Department of Justice]].

MDC Guaynabo is located next to [[Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico|Fort Buchanan]] U.S. Army base,<ref>"[https://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/gua/GUA_aohandbook.pdf Federal Bureau of Prisons Metropolitan Detention Center Guaynabo, Puerto Rico Unit Admission & Orientation Booklet 2011]." [[Bureau of Prisons]]. October 13, 2011. p. 7 (PDF p. 7/54). Retrieved on September 14, 2017.</ref> and is {{convert|6|mi|km}} west of San Juan, the capital of Puerto Rico.<ref>{{cite web|title=MDC Guaynabo|url=http://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/gua/index.jsp|publisher=Federal Bureau of Prisons}}</ref>

In the wake of the destruction of [[Hurricane Maria]] in September 2017, some 1200 federal prisoners were transferred from Guaynabo to the [[Federal Correctional Institution, Yazoo City]] in Mississippi.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gates |first1=Jimmie E. |title=State is housing 1,200 federal prisoners from Puerto Rico |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/news/2017/10/18/state-housing-1-200-federal-prisoners-puerto-rico/777228001/ |access-date=10 January 2019 |publisher=Clarion-Ledger (Jackson, Mississippi) |date=18 October 2017}}</ref>  Those 1200 were returned to Guaynabo in the first quarter of 2018, along with other prisoners who had been temporarily held in Atlanta, Georgia, Talladega Alabama, and Miami, Florida.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Speri |first1=Alice |title=PUERTO RICO WANTS TO CUT THE COST OF INCARCERATING PEOPLE BY SHIPPING THEM OFF THE ISLAND |url=https://theintercept.com/2018/03/23/puerto-rico-prisons-hurricane-maria/ |access-date=10 January 2019 |publisher=The Intercept |date=23 March 2018}}</ref>

==Notable incidents==
In 2010, an [[FBI]] investigation uncovered a conspiracy to distribute [[cocaine]], [[heroin]], [[marijuana]], [[Percocet]], and [[Xanax]] to an inmate at MDC Guaynabo. Several conspirators, led by Juan Rios-Ortiz, also attempted to provide cellular telephones, chargers, and [[SIM card]]s to an inmate of MDC. Rios-Ortiz worked for a company that had a contract to supply produce to the prison kitchen. Rios-Ortiz was subsequently convicted of [[conspiracy (crime)|conspiracy]] to distribute controlled substances, distribution of controlled substances, and providing contraband to an inmate of a federal prison.<ref>{{cite web|title=Juan Ríos Ortiz Found Guilty of Providing Contraband to the Federal Prison Defendant is Facing up to 20 Years in Prison and $1,000,000 in Fines|url=https://www.fbi.gov/sanjuan/press-releases/2010/sj111810.htm|publisher=Federal Bureau of Investigation|access-date=28 October 2013|date=November 18, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Inmate Locator - Juan Rios-Ortiz|url=http://www.bop.gov/iloc2/InmateFinderServlet?Transaction=IDSearch&needingMoreList=false&IDType=IRN&IDNumber=15853-069&x=86&y=18|publisher=Federal Bureau of Prisons|access-date=28 October 2013}}</ref>

On February 26, 2013, Osvaldo Albarati, a lieutenant for the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], was shot and killed in what is believed to be retaliation for his investigations into cellphone smuggling at MDC Guaynabo. He had just left the facility and was driving home when several gunmen opened fire on his vehicle on the De Diego Expressway near Bayamon.<ref>{{cite web|title=Federal corrections officer slain in Puerto Rico|url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/agencia-efe/130227/federal-corrections-officer-slain-puerto-rico|publisher=GlobalPost – International News|access-date=28 October 2013|date=February 27, 2013}}</ref>  Albarati worked in the investigative branch at the prison, where he was responsible for investigating crime within the prison, including drug smuggling and illegal cellphone use. Authorities have said his killing may have been contracted by powerful drug kingpins being held at the facility in reprisal for recent seizures he spearheaded.<ref>{{cite web|title=FBI: $50K reward in prison officer's slaying|url=http://www.caribbeanbusinesspr.com/news03.php?nt_id=82257&ct_id=1|publisher=Casiano Communications|access-date=28 October 2013|date=March 15, 2013|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029232436/http://www.caribbeanbusinesspr.com/news03.php?nt_id=82257&ct_id=1|archive-date=29 October 2013}}</ref> The [[FBI]] investigated the killing and no charges were filed.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lieutenant Osvaldo Albarati|url=http://www.odmp.org/officer/21764-lieutenant-osvaldo-albarati#ixzz2fZwUMVZv|publisher=Officer Down Memorial Page|access-date=28 October 2013}}</ref>

On March 24, 2020 as a result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Puerto Rico|COVID-19 pandemic]], the prison reported that it was operating on a modified schedule and inmates were not allowed visitors.<ref name="COVID-19">{{cite web |title=Bureau of Prisons Update on COVID-19 |url=https://www.bop.gov/resources/news/pdfs/20200324_bop_press_release_covid19_update.pdf |website=Bureau of Prisons |access-date=26 March 2020}}</ref>
